subject: Clarify July usage spike and proposed adjustment
messages:
From: Stardrift Billing <billing@stardrift.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ayesha Rao <ayesha@stardrift.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected July usage spike on invoice #RD-2027073

Hi David,

We received invoice RD-2027073 and noticed a ~4.8x increase in streaming token charges compared to June. The invoice shows a large line for streaming-generation tokens on the /v1/stream endpoint and an attachment (invoice_202707.pdf) is included for our AP team.

A few details:
- Account: Stardrift AI (entity in CA)
- Invoice period: 2027-07-01 to 2027-07-31
- Invoice total: $54,200 (we believe ~ $36,000 of that is unexpected streaming overage)

Can you provide a breakdown of the token aggregation methodology for streaming vs non-streaming calls, and check if any sampling/proration changed in July? We pulled a quick usage CSV and attached usage_export_202707.csv — there's a cluster of sessions around 2027-07-16 that look like automated test runs but the tokens counted are orders of magnitude higher than the session logs in our app.

This is holding up our payment (AP has put the invoice on review) — we need an explanation and proposed remediation by EOD next Wednesday (2027-09-08) for our internal auditors. Also confirm whether any credit will be gross of VAT or if we'll need an amended invoice reflecting VAT impact.

Thanks,
Ayesha Rao
Head of Finance — Stardrift AI
billing@stardrift.ai

Attachment: usage_export_202707.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)
Attachment: invoice_202707.pdf (PDF, 280KB)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Stardrift Billing <billing@stardrift.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected July usage spike on invoice #RD-2027073

Ayesha, thanks for flagging — we appreciate the attachments and the quick context.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- I’ve looped in Ben (AE) and Karthik (Billing Ops) to pull detailed telemetry and cross-check the streaming token accounting for July.
- We’ll compare your exported session IDs to our request logs and the aggregation window used by our metering pipeline (hourly bucketing vs. rolling-window sampling).
- If we identify an overcount, we’ll calculate a proposed credit and provide a revised invoice (including VAT treatment) and a short adjustment statement for your auditors.

Can you confirm the HubSpot ticket id (if you created one) or the preferred place to send the show-back CSV and proofing docs? I’ll aim to have an interim update by EOD Monday (2027-09-06) and a proposed credit by Wednesday.

Best,
David Kim
Director, Customer Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Sep 4, 2027 at 09:12 Stardrift Billing <billing@stardrift.ai> wrote:
> (original message)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stardrift Billing <billing@stardrift.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2027 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected July usage spike on invoice #RD-2027073 — initial findings

David / Karthik / Ayesha — quick initial findings from our ops review. Attaching a small diff (usage_diff_202707_adjustment.csv) that maps Stardrift's session ids to our request ids and token tallies.

What we found (summary):
- Root cause: a streaming-session-termination race in our 2027-06 runtime patch caused an extra finalization event to be recorded for multi-chunk streaming sessions when a client closed a connection within the same second as the final chunk. That finalization path committed the partial buffer twice into the metering pipeline in rare cases.
- Scope: ~2.6% of streaming sessions in July for Stardrift were affected, but those sessions were long-lived batch-ish streams used by one internal test harness — they had very high token counts per session so the dollar impact is magnified.
- Numbers: our corrected tally for July streaming-generation tokens for your account is 1,420,158 tokens (reconciled) vs 1,724,930 tokens on the billed invoice — proposed gross credit: $12,480 (before VAT).

Notes on methodology:
- We used your supplied usage_export_202707.csv to match session UUIDs. We then reprocessed matching request logs through a corrected aggregation step (no double-finalize), and re-ran our billing tally. Full proofing is in the attached CSV.
- Sampling/proration: there was no intentional sampling config change on 2027-07-01; the counts above are from production metering with the known bug.

Proposed remediation:
1) Issue a credit of $12,480 gross (line item credit on a revised invoice).
2) Provide a credit memo and an amended invoice reflecting VAT reversal for your auditors (we’ll confirm your VAT registration details and whether to treat as reverse charge).
3) Offer one-time account credit of $3,000 as a customer goodwill gesture (applied to next invoice).

Action items:
- Ayesha: confirm you accept the proposed credit and whether you need the amendment to show VAT separately or net.
- Karthik: please prepare the credit memo and draft amended invoice (PDF) and confirm VAT handling.
- David: I’ll coordinate the proofing CSV and the BigQuery export link for your records.

Attachment: usage_diff_202707_adjustment.csv (CSV, 240KB)
Link: https://console.cloud.google.com/bigquery?project=redwood-prod&d=usage_export&p=redwood-prod&t=stardrift_202707

Ben Carter
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ayesha Rao <ayesha@stardrift.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2027 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected July usage spike on invoice #RD-2027073 — acceptance of credit

Thanks — appreciate the quick triage and the clear breakdown. We accept the proposed $12,480 gross credit and the additional $3,000 goodwill credit. Two quick clarifications for our records/audit: 

1) VAT handling: Stardrift is VAT registered in the EU for a subsidiary; for this US-entity invoice we need the credit memo to show the original VAT line and the reversal amount so our EU tax team can map cross-entity adjustments. Please include VAT at 0% and a separate VAT reversal line if applicable. If you need our VAT registration numbers, we’ll provide them via the HubSpot ticket (preferred).

2) Adjustment statement: we require a short signed adjustment statement (1 page) stating the root cause, the corrected token counts and the gross/net credit applied. This will be included in our internal audit packet.

If you can get the amended invoice + credit memo + signed adjustment statement to billing@stardrift.ai and upload to the HubSpot ticket by COB Monday (2027-09-06), we’ll release the payment for the remaining balance.

Best regards,
Ayesha Rao
Head of Finance — Stardrift AI
